response: Research has shown that there is a gender difference in the survival of resected non-small cell lung cancer, but this difference is primarily observed in the adenocarcinoma subset. Studies have found that women tend to have better survival rates than men, but this advantage is not seen when comparing propensity-matched gender pairs. This suggests that the pathobiology of adenocarcinoma in women may be different from that of men, leading to a more favorable outcome for women with this specific type of non-small cell lung cancer.
